record.original_question: Can nonstationary generalized minimal flows in two-dimensional Euler dynamics have dynamics more complicated than time-periodic or quasiperiodic motion, for example chaotic behavior?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on a closed surface (for instance the flat 2-torus), regarded as a geodesic equation on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with respect to the L^2 metric. A generalized flow (in the sense of Brenier) is a probability measure on the space of particle paths whose one-time marginal at every time is the volume form and which is a critical point of the kinetic-energy action functional between prescribed initial and final particle configurations; a generalized minimal flow is one realizing the infimum of the action. Such a generalized flow is called nonstationary if its velocity field depends on time. Known examples of nonstationary generalized minimal flows on the 2-torus consist of several vortex blobs that move and change shape, exhibiting time-periodic or quasiperiodic behavior. 

Question: Do there exist nonstationary generalized minimal flows for the two-dimensional Euler dynamics whose time evolution is more complicated than periodic or quasiperiodic motion — for example, chaotic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is identified as an open problem in geometric hydrodynamics. The recent work of Izosimov and Khesin (Calc. Var. PDE, 2024; arXiv:2206.01434) on generalized fluid flows describes nonstationary generalized minimal flows with vortex blobs exhibiting (quasi)periodic motion and explicitly states that whether more complex/chaotic dynamics can occur is unclear. No resolution was found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of generalized fluid flows
status_evidence.snippet: Nonstationary generalized minimal flows on the torus comprise several vortex blobs moving and changing shape; these appear (quasi)periodic and it is unclear whether they can be chaotic.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether nonstationary generalized minimal flows in 2D Euler dynamics can exhibit chaotic behavior remains open.

status_evidence.title: Problems in geometric hydrodynamics (Khesin)
status_evidence.snippet: It is unclear whether such generalized minimal flows can have more complicated dynamics than time-periodic or quasiperiodic motion.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in geometric hydrodynamics.
